label: Atelier Coatings & Tools synthetic three-statement and DCF
prompt: Build a five-year annual integrated three-statement model and exit-multiple DCF for the fictional, synthetic EUR company Atelier Coatings & Tools S.A. It has two business lines: manufactured colored paint and purchased/resold painting tools. Opening historical balance sheet: cash EUR 1.5m, receivables EUR 2.2m, inventory EUR 3.5m, net PP&E EUR 12.8m, total assets EUR 20.0m, accounts payable EUR 2.0m, other current liabilities EUR 0.5m, term debt EUR 10.0m (exactly 50% of total assets), revolver EUR 0.0m, and equity EUR 7.5m. Starting operations: 400,000 paint units at EUR 32 per unit with EUR 14 variable production cost per unit and EUR 1.5m manufacturing overhead; 300,000 tools units at EUR 18 per unit with EUR 10 purchase cost per unit and EUR 0.6m storage/logistics expense; consolidated operating expenses EUR 3.0m. Make separate unit growth, price inflation and unit-cost inflation assumptions editable for each line, together with receivable, inventory and payable days, annual capex, mandatory term-debt amortization, a 25% tax rate, 6% cash interest expense on average total debt, 2% interest income on average cash above the EUR 1.0m minimum cash balance, and a 50% optional excess-cash sweep. Apply sweep capacity first to outstanding revolver and then to term debt, prohibit simultaneous draw and sweep, and draw the revolver when cash would otherwise fall below minimum cash. Resolve any cash/debt/interest circularity deterministically and expose a convergence residual. Preserve the reported opening working-capital balances, calculate a days-based normalized opening reference using revenue for receivables and consistent COGS for inventory and payables, and disclose the Year 1 normalization as a separate one-time cash-flow component rather than recurring operating improvement. Treat opening net PP&E as a separate pool with a 10-year remaining life. Depreciate new capex straight-line over 10 years using a half-year convention. Define the 1% annual disposal assumption as retirement of fully depreciated gross cost with exactly matching accumulated depreciation: it reduces gross PP&E and accumulated depreciation equally, has zero net-book-value, no proceeds, no gain/loss, no cash-flow effect, and must never be added to depreciation or FCFF. Do not model impairment. Produce segment units, prices, revenue, variable costs, gross profit and margins; consolidated EBITDA, EBIT, interest expense, interest income, taxes and net income; linked income statements, balance sheets and cash-flow statements; working-capital normalization, PP&E, term debt, revolver, interest and retained-earnings schedules; cash-flow reconciliation and balance-sheet checks; FCFF; an exit-multiple DCF using 9% WACC and 6.0x terminal EBITDA; WACC sensitivity from 7%-11% and exit multiple sensitivity from 5.0x-7.0x; and an enterprise-to-equity bridge. Do not use a perpetuity-growth terminal value and do not silently floor negative terminal EBITDA at zero. Keep base, downside and upside scenarios for backend execution and model stability/direction tests only; do not manufacture cross-scenario values inside a single-case output. All quantities, prices, costs, capex and balances must reject negative or non-finite values. Growth and inflation must be bounded from -50% to +100%; working-capital days 0-365; tax 0-50%; interest rates and WACC 0-30%; terminal multiple 0-15x; cash sweep 0-100%; useful lives 1-40 years; and disposal rate 0-25%. Legitimate zero inputs must not crash or create NaN/infinity; undefined ratios should be null or clearly not applicable. Reusable checks must validate current-case identities and must not hardcode EUR 20.0m assets, 50% leverage, a zero-draw Base case, or saved scenario values. Make all key outputs and schedules available to outputs.py for the existing ad hoc presentation without recalculating financial mechanics there.
prompt_complexity: two-segment integrated three-statement forecast with normalized working capital, term debt and revolver mechanics, PP&E vintages, exit-multiple DCF, and independent checks
notes: Synthetic live showcase fixture only; not deterministic product template logic.
